title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
Improved monitoring of Bilateral Agreements (BLAs) and Memorandum of Understanding (MOUs) between Ethiopia and destination countries. In 2021, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs developed an online cloud based monitoring system to follow up on the implementation of BLAs and MoUs. The online system provides practical and effective electronic monitoring mechanism to support signatories to follow up on the implementation of BLAs and MoUs. They system enable the Ethiopian diplomatic mission to feed information based on the cases being filed by migrant workers, it helps the Ethiopian diplomatic issue to better follow up on pending issues. The system will also help generate reports on cases that are in breach of the BLA signed between Ethiopia and the Country of Destination to help address this issue on the quarterly or biannual joint committee meetings.
In 2021, the Job Creation commission (JCC) drafted and negotiated an MOU ready for final review and signature with Workforce Connexon in UAE, with an intention to facilitate employment opportunity for around 50,000 Ethiopian migrants to UAE. MOU was also signed between the Ministry of Health, JCC and Response Plus to recruit thousands of Health Care Professionals through a circular migration program. An agreement was also reached with UAE Ministry of Education to sign MOU with the government of Ethiopia on areas of educational standards, equivalency and professional competency certifications. In 2021, the GoE is finalizing the BLA with Bahrain for the protection of migrant workers. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the Government of Ethiopia in developing online monitoring tool for the implementation of Bilateral Agreements (BLAs) and Memorandum of Understandings (MOUs). The ILO supported the design, development and implementation of the online monitoring system, by providing technical and financial support as well as in coordinating input from relevant actors in the design process. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the Government of Ethiopia multi-disciplinary mission to UAE to discuss the MoU's. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO provided technical inputs based on ILS in the drafting of a BLA between the GoE and Bahrain.

title.narrative: 7.5.3. Number of bilateral or regional labour migration frameworks, with monitoring and review mechanisms to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
In 2020-21, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has provided new services to protect Ethiopian migrant workers affected by COVID-19 in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Lebanon. The services include shelter for migrant workers (1,277) awareness creation (26,362) and legal support (182) to claim unpaid wages (USD 349,102). The Ethiopian Diplomatic mission and Community in Lebanon and UAE have established a training centre where Ethiopian migrants can take skill development courses..
In 2021, the Government of Ethiopia under the leadership of the National Council Chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister of Ethiopia launched a national mobilization campaign to promote regular migration and combat irregular migration.
In 2020-21, around 1,500,000 potential migrants, migrants, returnees, Private Employment Agencies (PrEAS) and the general public's awareness was raised on labour migration issues ,through: dissemination of brochures in Ethiopia and key country of destination; dissemination of a Code of Conduct for PrEAs; broadcasting of the movie "Sewentwa", (a comparative story on the positive aspects of labour migration and the adverse effects of irregular migration) through TV stations, Migrant information Centres (MICs), ILO Youtube and Diretube. MoLSA is administering a new mobile app (YeGuzo Sink), which provides information on the overall migration process, including pre-departure, departure, deployment and return and reintegration.
In 2020, Migrant information centre (MIC) managed by the Bureau of Labour and Social Affairs in Agaro, Areka, Jeri, Sekota, Tulu Bolo and Wukro improved service for migrants, including, access to information, and available services and referral for returned migrants. In 2021, 2,958 potential migrant workers were trained on core skills, including entrepreneurship and financial education. Some of these potential migrants have already received job offer in KSA and UAE in the health sector. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to support the diplomatic missions to assist migrant workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. The ILO further capacitated the Ethiopian Consulates by providing training materials for the migrant training centres in Beirut and Dubai. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the national mobilization Campaign through shaping and forming the content of the conference, sharing the global and regional migration trends and organizing the conference in partnership with MoLSA.
With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the development, promotion and dissemination of all the awareness-raising materials, including the brochures, movie and mobile app.
With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, in 2020, the ILO supported strengthening the capacity of six Migrant Information Centre (MICs) by developing an Operational Manual for the MICs and translating it into Amharic, Afan Oromo & Tigrigna, providing training for the MICs staff and by procuring relevant equipment's to facilitate the day-to-day work of the MICs With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, in 2020, the ILO partnered with private and public training institutions and provided training for 2,958 potential migrants on core skills, as well as entrepreneurship and financial education.

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of countries with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
In October 2019, the Government of Ethiopia under the leadership of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) initiated the amendment process of the Ethiopian Overseas Employment Proclamation 923/2016. After several consultation with all relevant partners including social partners (employers' federation and trade unions), in May 2021, the Parliament adopted the amendment of the Ethiopia's Overseas Employment proclamation 1246/2021 and entered into force in June 2021. The amendment proclamation adds new and amended some provisions. The amended proclamation incorporate changes to include different skills set of migrants and broaden destination countries beyond the traditional Middle East countries, it also amended the minimum educational level requirement; requirement of BLA; requirement of training as long as they have the required certification and established Ethiopian Overseas Employment Board to be led by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs.
In January 2019, the Government of Ethiopia under the leadership of the Attorney General Office initiated the amendment of Proclamation 909/2015 on Prevention and Suppression of Trafficking in person and Smuggling of migrants. After several consultation with relevant partners, in February 2020, the Parliament approved the proclamation 1178/2020, which entered into force in March 2020. The amendment of proclamation 909/2015 was needed in order to clarify the scope and definition of terms, introduce links articulated with the criminal code, and put in place a framework on how to prevent Ethiopian citizens from the causes of trafficking and smuggling. With the support of the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the Government of Ethiopia in the revision of Overseas employment proclamation 1246/2021, through providing technical inputs based on ILS and sharing of experiences of other countries of origin. The ILO also translated the proclamation from Amharic to English to be presented to the Council of Ministers and the Parliament. Moreover, after the adoption of the proclamation, the ILO in partnership with MoLSA organized 6 sensitizations workshop throughout the country to ensure key stakeholders are aware of the new provisions and their implications. The ILO further got the new proclamation printed and disseminated to ensure it reached all relevant stakeholders.
With assistance from the Government of the United Kingdom, the ILO supported the Government of Ethiopia in the revision of Prevention and Suppression of Trafficking in person and Smuggling of migrants Proclamation 1178/2020, through providing technical inputs. After the adoption of the proclamation, the ILO in partnership with Attorney General Office (AGO) organized 6 sensitizations workshop throughout the country to ensure key stakeholders are aware of the new provisions and their implications. The ILO also supported the development of the three years Strategic Plan of the National Partnership Coalition (Coordination mechanism established by the proclamation), by providing technical inputs as well as bringing together relevant actors to develop the plan. Moreover, ILO supported the AGO in the evaluation of the National Partnership coalition performance for 2020/21.
